name: Knock-Out Whist
description: Trick-taking game where players drop out when they take no tricks. Each round has one fewer card per player (7 down to 1). Trump is turned in the first hand; thereafter the winner of the previous hand chooses trumps. Last player standing wins.

overview.description: Trick-taking game where players drop out when they take no tricks. Each round has one fewer card per player (7 down to 1). Trump is turned in the first hand; thereafter the winner of the previous hand chooses trumps. Last player standing wins.

history.origins: Knock-Out Whist is a simple plain-trick whist variant, often played as a children's game but with enough tactics for adult play, sometimes for small stakes. In Britain it is called Knockout Whist or Trumps; in North America it is also known as Scrounge or Rat.
timeline: 20th century: plain-trick whist variant documented as children's and pub game in Britain and North America.
history.cultural: Popular in Britain and North America as a family and pub game.
history.evolution: Session of seven hands of diminishing size (7 to 1 card each) with knockout elimination.

setup.dealing: Dealer deals seven cards each (first hand), clockwise. Uppermost undealt card is turned face up for trump. Subsequent hands: six cards each, then five, four, three, two, one. Winner of previous hand chooses trump after looking at their cards; on a tie, players cut for the right to choose.

rules.objective: Be the last player remaining by avoiding taking zero tricks in any hand; players who take no tricks are knocked out. Win the final one-trick hand or be the sole survivor.
rules.gameplay: Player to dealer's left leads. Must follow suit if able; otherwise any card. Highest trump wins the trick, else highest card of the led suit. Trick winner leads next. A player who takes no tricks is knocked out (first such player gets one dog's life hand of one card). Seven hands per game with 7, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1 cards dealt respectively.
keyRules: Highest trump in trick wins; otherwise highest card of led suit.
Trick winner leads to the next trick.
Zero tricks in a hand knocks you out; first time only you get a dog's life (one card next hand).
Winner of most tricks chooses trumps for next hand; tie resolved by cutting.

strategy.basic: Choose trumps: pick your longest suit. From equal-length suits, prefer the one without very high cards (they may win tricks off-suit).
strategy.intermediate: Track trumps and leads to avoid taking tricks when you need to survive. On a dog's life, save your card for a trick you can win.
strategy.advanced: Count cards and manage knock-out risk each round; coordinate with hand size (fewer cards means fewer ways to dump losers).
tips: Make hearts (or your longest suit) trumps when you have length.
Do not choose a suit full of high cards as trump; they win anyway.

variations.name: Winner deals and leads
variations.description: From the second deal onwards, the winner of the previous hand also deals and leads to the first trick. Some play that the dealer leads in the first deal.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant changes dealer and lead only; engine overrides could be added when implementing.

variations.name: Card exchange
variations.description: After trumps are chosen, each player may discard 1, 2 or 3 cards and receive that many replacements (all at once). When only 2 or 1 card is dealt, only 1 or 2 can be discarded.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant adds pre-play exchange; engine deal or draw logic would need overrides.

variations.name: No dog's life
variations.description: Anyone who takes no trick is immediately out; no dog's life hand.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant removes dog's life rule; edge case and round logic would need overrides.

variations.name: Options when choosing trumps
variations.description: Winner may choose no trump, aces high or low, and normal or reverse ranking (low card takes).
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant adds trump and ranking options; trumpConfig overrides could be added.

variations.name: 2 of diamonds
variations.description: The 2 of diamonds counts as permanent highest trump, above the ace of trumps.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant adds permanent highest trump; special card or trump overrides would be needed.

scoring.description: No points; players are eliminated when they take no tricks in a hand. First such player gets one dog's life; thereafter elimination is immediate.
scoring.winCondition: Last player standing wins; or winner of the one trick in the final (one-card) hand.
